subject: Post-call: PayMesh discovery — token burn, batching levers & pilot runway
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ramos <sofia.ramos@paymesh.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 25 Sep 2026 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: PayMesh discovery — token burn, batching levers & pilot runway

Hi Sofia — great to connect today, appreciate the time. Quick recap from our call plus suggested next steps so we’re aligned. I pulled the key pain points and an initial TCO sketch (high level) — attaching a short spreadsheet and the pilot statement.

Summary of pain points you shared:
- Token volatility: multi-turn reconciliations + customer chats spike token usage at month-end, causing unpredictable bills.
- Throughput constraints: real-time reconciliation flows need sub-300ms tails during peak windows.
- Budget cap: Finance has signaled a hard ceiling around ~$75k/quarter for inference (proof-of-value period).
- Compliance: logs retention and SSO/SCIM are gating checks for procurement.

Goals (what success looks like):
- Predictable per-ticket inference cost <= $0.03 within pilot scope.
- Sustained 99th pctl latency < 300ms for reconciliation API calls.
- Demonstrable 30–40% TCO reduction via batching/caching and cheaper model fallbacks while preserving quality.

Levers we can apply (what we’d test during a 4–8 week pilot):
1) Batching + async workers for bulk reconciliation jobs — expect 20–30% token savings on those flows.
2) Prefix/KV caching on common prompts (customer metadata + templates) — reduces repeated token generation for multi-step flows.
3) Model routing policy: use a cheaper, quantized variant for high-throughput, low-risk paths and full model for critical decisioning.
4) Committed Dedicated capacity option to stabilize latency at scale and reduce unit cost.

Initial back-of-envelope TCO (monthly, illustrative):
- Current baseline (estimated): 10M tokens/mo -> ~$12.0k/mo (existing vendor)
- Redwood hosted, no optimizations: ~9.2k/mo
- Redwood + batching/caching (40% token reduction on applicable flows): ~5.5k/mo
- Redwood + 6-mo commit (Dedicated) + ops runbook: ~4.2k/mo
=> Estimated pilot savings window: 35–65% depending on scope and commit. Attached spreadsheet has scenarios broken down by flow.

Asks / next steps:
- Can you confirm the hard budget ceiling for the pilot (you mentioned $75k/quarter) so I can size the pilot commit and recommended capacity?
- Please introduce the procurement owner (you mentioned Ravi Patel) so we can align on SOC2, SSO/SCIM, and contract milestones.
- If that’s good, propose a 30–45 minute kickoff next week (technical + ops) — I called out Wed 10:00am PT below as a candidate.

Attachments: paymesh_tco_scenarios.xlsx (TCO scenarios), redwood_pilot_statement.pdf (pilot scope + SLAs)

Thanks — I’ll hold open Wed 10:00am PT for a kickoff unless you prefer another time.

—
Marissa Cole

Subject: Re: Post-call: PayMesh discovery — token burn, batching levers & pilot runway

Thanks Marissa — useful summary and I appreciate the concrete numbers. A few quick notes: 

- Budget: confirmed — Finance has allocated up to $75k for a Q1 pilot but it needs approval from Ravi (Head of Ops).
- Use cases: the big wins would be reconciliation (nightly bulk) and the customer support assistant (multi-turn chat). Those are the two flows to focus on for batching + KV caching.
- Compliance: please send SOC2 Type II report and an SSO/SCIM integration doc — procurement will need that before we spin up any private capacity.

Can you also break down the "Redwood + batching/caching" line into per-flow savings in the spreadsheet? For example, what % of the 40% comes from reconciliation vs. chat?

I’m looping in Ravi (ravi.patel@paymesh.com) — Ravi, Marissa is sharing pilot TCO and suggested next steps; can you confirm the procurement checklist and whether legal needs to own the initial SOW review?

If it helps, Wed 10:00am PT works for me.

Thanks Sofia — looping Ravi in as requested and attaching a slightly expanded spreadsheet that breaks down savings per flow (reconciliation vs support chat) and the pilot statement for procurement.

Quick notes on the per-flow breakout (see attachment tab "Flow scenarios"):
- Reconciliation (batch): ~55% of the modeled savings comes from batching because we can shift the work to large inference batches in off-peak windows and enable prefix caching for repeated templates.
- Support chat (multi-turn): ~30% savings from KV caching + model routing (cheaper quantized model for non-critical responses).
- Misc / other flows: ~15% (routing + token-level prompt edits).

SOC2 and SSO/SCIM docs: here are two links to the artifacts procurement will need: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-paymesh-pilot (contains SOC2 summary, SSO integration guide, and sample SOW).

Proposed pilot kickoff: Wed, 29 Sep 2026, 10:00am PT (30–45 min). Agenda: 1) Goals & scope, 2) Instrumentation & metrics, 3) Timeline & success criteria, 4) Procurement checklist. I’ll send a calendar invite and include the pilot statement.
